description:
Found while writing JMAP-hwdv.7 integration tests.

handle_task_list_set (crate-jmap-tasks-server/src/task_list.rs) does not check backend.account_exists before processing the /set request. When the accountId is unknown, the handler silently 'succeeds' with a fake oldState/newState envelope and creates objects against the nonexistent account (which the MemoryBackend then auto-registers — its silent-auto-register defense is what made this visible).

RFC 8620 §3.6.2 mandates a method-level accountNotFound error when accountId is not recognised.

Reproduction:
```rust
let backend = MemoryBackend::new(); // no accounts registered
let args = json!({"accountId": "nobody", "create": {"c1": {"name": "x"}}});
let result = handle_task_list_set(&backend, args).await;
// Expected: Err(JmapError::AccountNotFound)
// Actual:   Ok((response_envelope_with_notCreated_invalidProperties, _))
```

Same pattern was previously fixed for calendars-server as JMAP-r3pg.4. This is the tasks-server sibling of that bug.

Also likely affects: Task/set, TaskNotification/set, Task/copy. Audit all four.

The corresponding ignored test in crate-jmap-tasks-server/tests/tasks_tests.rs is task_list_set_unknown_account_returns_account_not_found.
title: P1: TaskList/set missing accountId existence check (RFC 8620 §3.6.2)
